To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the optimal restructuring strategy is a mix of interest payment concessions and nominal value haircuts; 2) the interest payment concessions are more effective when applied to the most recent debt issues; 3) the interest payment concession strategy has the advantage of reducing the debt service costs in the short-term and of being less risky in the long-term.

the optimal solution of the stochastic programming model is a debt restructuring plan that minimizes the expected present value of the debt service payments, while keeping the conditional Debt-at-Risks below the specified risk limits.

, while the debt crisis in Greece was not inevitable, it was unavoidable.
the Greek debt is unsustainable.
a debt restructuring is necessary, but not sufficient to restore debt sustainability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while debt restructuring is an important policy tool, it is not a panacea for sovereign debt crises and it is not a substitute for a proper macroeconomic policy.
, in order to restore debt sustainability, the debt-to-GDP should be reduced to about 60% of GDP in the long run.
, in the case of a sovereign debt crisis, debt restructuring is not only necessary but also unavoidable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal restructuring of sovereign debt should be based on a comprehensive assessment of the debt portfolio and its risk profile, rather than a piecemeal approach.
a debt restructuring program is not a one-time operation but rather a continuous and dynamic process.
a combination of interest payment concessions and maturity rescheduling, with a haircut on nominal value is needed to restore debt sustainability and avoid a debt restructuring.
